model_interpretation.claim: Factoring the shared permutation prefixes across the eight corner hashes may reduce redundant scalar table lookups in each Noise call while leaving gradient arithmetic, interpolation, and octave control flow unchanged. The compiler may already perform some common-subexpression elimination, so this is a measurable hypothesis, not an assumed speedup; compare correctness and timing against baseline-e1.

items.subject: Scalar Perlin hash, gradient, and interpolation kernel
items.objective: Test scalar-only restructuring of the per-pixel Noise/Grad path. Measure hash-addressing/gradient-selection changes separately from interpolation-polynomial and octave-control-flow changes, so the source of any gain or regression is visible. Use the original scalar implementation as the controlled comparison; correctness-preserving combinations remain possible but should be measured separately. Validate all specified checks and the fixed tolerance, and record failed approaches. Do not assume arithmetic rewrites or table changes will be faster.
